headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow corruption plausible by default; compliance risk is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests files, browsers, and MCP/API outputs, while kestra can pass workflow inputs, logs, and messages between tasks. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Kestra feeds gpt-researcher untrusted content or if gpt-researcher writes artifacts Kestra later parses. No explicit provenance controls are shown in either profile.
conditions: IF Kestra passes untrusted workflow inputs or logs into gpt-researcher prompts
IF gpt-researcher output is later parsed as instructions by Kestra tasks
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and schema validator for all agent-to-agent text
Strip imperative language from inputs before prompting gpt-researcher
Require human review before Kestra executes any LLM-generated step
Log and reject outputs that contain workflow-control keywords
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read access; gpt-researcher also handles local documents and secrets, while kestra can write files and move data through logs, messages, cloud storage, and notifications. In a shared workspace, sensitive research inputs can flow into Kestra outputs or external services without a default containment boundary.
conditions: IF both agents share any filesystem path or mounted workspace
IF Kestra forwards agent outputs to Slack, email, cloud storage, or external APIs
IF gpt-researcher is given documents containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount only read-only inputs
Disable external notifications for sensitive runs
Use per-agent service accounts and distinct API keys
Redact secrets before gpt-researcher reads documents
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on Kestra outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files and spawn subprocesses, and kestra can execute shell, write files, and also spawn subprocesses. If they operate on the same directory or shared artifacts, concurrent writes and workflow-state corruption are likely, especially because both support multiple instances and no locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store
IF Kestra tasks and gpt-researcher instances run concurrently on shared state
IF either agent mutates git or workflow files without locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make shared artifacts read-only after generation
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a content-writing/research agent that can generate citations and reports, and kestra is an automation orchestrator with email, Slack, and cloud actions. If Kestra treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, a bad citation or fabricated fact can cascade into downstream notifications or operational tasks without verification.
conditions: IF Kestra uses gpt-researcher output as an input to automated tasks
IF no verification step checks citations or factual claims before execution
IF downstream tasks send notifications or modify infrastructure
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action task
Require citation checks for all generated claims
Route outputs to a human approval queue
Limit Kestra to read-only reporting for LLM outputs
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents, citations, and secrets, while kestra handles logs, messages, cloud storage, and notifications. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is moved from research inputs into orchestration logs or external channels. No compliance controls are documented in either profile, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in gpt-researcher inputs
IF Kestra logs or notifies on the same data class
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the workflow
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from orchestration logs
Mask identifiers before passing data to Kestra
Set short retention on workflow logs
Use region-scoped storage and notification endpoints
requires-engineering: document and enforce a data-handling policy
